summary.one_liner: A browser-based Markdown review tool, packaged as a single HTML file plus a CLI and a Claude Code skill, that exports inline reviewer comments as structured JSON keyed by heading path and source line.
summary.what_it_does: Renders a Markdown file in a single standalone HTML page where a reviewer can select text ranges and leave inline comments. Comments export as JSON with headingPath and sourceLine fields so an LLM can apply them to exact locations. The CLI (npx mdxg-redline) generates a review HTML next to the input file and opens it in the browser, with options for hiding the comments panel, choosing the output directory, and controlling Shiki, Mermaid and KaTeX injection. An md-review skill lets an agent request a review and pick up the feedback JSON from a shared folder. The viewer supports virtual stacked pages, WASD keyboard navigation, footnotes, math, Mermaid diagrams and code highlighting. A --clean subcommand removes generated review and feedback file pairs.
use_cases: reviewing AI-written documentation before accepting it
leaving inline comments on a Markdown spec for an LLM to revise
round-trip review loop between an agent and a human reviewer
reading Markdown files in a browser as a plain viewer
sharing a single offline HTML file for document review
how_to_run: gh skill install oubakiou/mdxg-redline md-review --agent claude-code --scope project
npx skills add oubakiou/mdxg-redline --skill md-review --agent claude-code --yes
notable: Ships as a single standalone HTML file that runs fully in the browser with no server required
Exports comments as JSON keyed by headingPath and sourceLine so changes target exact lines
Claude Code skill (md-review) that polls for the feedback file in a shared folder
Implements the MDXG Viewer profile of the Markdown Experience Guidelines, with math, Mermaid and footnote extensions
Hides open-file and paste options by default so reloading does not discard comments
caveats: Writing feedback.json directly relies on the File System Access API, so only Chromium-based browsers support it; Safari and Firefox must use download or clipboard export
Third-party implementation, not affiliated with Vercel Labs or the upstream mdxg repository; MDXG spec is a preview and may change
Random fallback ports in dev containers may not reach the host browser unless MDXG_REDLINE_PORT is pinned or forwarded
